en: The Biography of Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
There was a great master named Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa, who was a disciple of the Elder Pārśva. At that time, the Elder...
With diligent effort and concern for the Buddha-dharma, he entered a samādhi of contemplation,
wondering who would be capable of leaving the household life to widely proclaim the transformative teachings of the Way and awaken sentient beings.
He saw that there was a renunciant non-Buddhist practitioner in Central India.
He was a man of worldly wisdom and sharp eloquence, well-versed in debate,
who proclaimed: "If there are any bhikṣus who can debate with me..."
One may strike the *gandī* bell;
however, if one is unable to do so,
it is improper to publicly ring the *gandī* and accept the offerings of others.
At that time, the Elder Pārśva was setting out from Northern India, intending to travel to China;
there was a city named Śākya.
On the road he encountered several śrāmaṇeras who all teased him together,
saying, "Venerable Elder, give us your *pūrala*."
There were then those who took him away and tormented him in various ways, treating him with utter lack of reason;
yet the Elder Pārśva maintained an unchanged expression on his face, remaining serene and unperturbed.
Among the śrāmaṇeras, those who were extensively learned perceived his profound and vast nature and suspected he was no ordinary man;
they questioned him and observed his conduct.
He answered every question exhaustively and proceeded without ceasing;
his countenance was profound and far-reaching, never dwelling on the trivial or mundane.
At that time, the śrāmaṇeras fully observed that the elder’s virtue and capacity were deep and vast.
Knowing that he was unfathomable, they redoubled their reverence and all together escorted him.
Thus it was with the Elder Pārśva.
Immediately, by means of his supernormal power, he ascended into the air and traveled to Central India.
Staying at a monastery, he asked the bhikṣus,
"Why do you not strike the ghaṇṭā according to the Dharma?"
The bhikṣus said,
"Venerable Mahāla, there is a reason why he does not strike you."
He asked, "For what reason?
and he replied,
"There is a renunciant non-Buddhist who is highly skilled in debate."
He issued a proclamation throughout the kingdom to the assembly of Śākya sons and śramaṇas:
"If you are unable to engage me in debate,
you shall not publicly strike the *ghanṭā* to receive the offerings of others."
Because of these words, he did not strike [the gong].
The Elder Pārśva said,
"Simply ring the *ghanṭā*."
"If he should come, I myself will confront him.
The senior bhikṣus were deeply amazed by these words,
yet they were doubtful and unable to discern their meaning.
They gathered together to deliberate, saying, "Let us first strike the *ghanṭā*.
If the non-Buddhists come,
we shall let the Elder do as he pleases."
He immediately struck the *ghanṭā*.
The non-Buddhists then asked,
"For what reason do you strike this wooden instrument today?"
He replied,
"There is an elder śramaṇa in the north who came to strike the *ghanṭā*; it was not we."
The non-Buddhist said, "Let him come; we shall go out to meet him.
They immediately went out and met one another.
The non-Buddhist asked,
"Do you wish to engage in debate?
He replied, "Indeed."
The non-Buddhist immediately laughed in derision and said,
"Since this elder bhikṣu’s physical appearance is such as this,
he speaks again."
"You are no ordinary man.
How can you wish to debate with me?
He then made a mutual agreement.
"Seven days from now,
you shall assemble the kings, ministers, śramaṇas, tīrthikas,
and all the great Dharma masters here for this debate."
On the night of the sixth day, the Elder lay on his side and entered into *samādhi* to observe what was appropriate.
At dawn on the seventh day, the great assembly gathered like clouds.
The Elder arrived first and immediately ascended the high seat;
his countenance was serene and joyful, twice as radiant as usual.
The non-Buddhists arrived later and sat down before him.
He observed that the śramaṇa’s countenance was harmonious and joyful, and his mind was peaceful and at ease;
furthermore, his entire body was endowed with the marks of a great man.
He then thought to himself, "Could this not be a holy bhikṣu?"
His mind was peaceful and joyful, and he further elaborated on the characteristics of marks.
Today, an excellent discourse is about to be established.
They then made a mutual agreement: "If one should fall into defeat, what punishment shall there be? The non-Buddhist said, "If one should be defeated, his tongue shall be cut out."
The Elder Pārśva said, "This is not permissible;
it is sufficient for you to act as a disciple to fulfill the agreement.
He replied, "So be it."
He asked again, "Who should speak first?
The Elder Pārśva replied,
"Since I am advanced in years, I have come from afar."
Furthermore, since you were previously seated here, you ought to have spoken first.
The non-Buddhists may say, "That is indeed so;
we shall now completely refute everything you have said."
The Elder Pārśva immediately said,
"May the world be brought to great peace, may the Great King enjoy long life, and may the land be prosperous and joyful, free from all calamities and afflictions.
The non-Buddhists remained silent, not knowing what to say.
To argue that phenomena are non-resistant is to fall into a point of defeat.
He humbled himself to serve as a disciple, having his hair and beard shaved;
he was ordained as a śrāmaṇera and received full ordination.
Sitting alone in one place, he thought to himself:
"My talent is brilliant, my far-reaching insight resounds throughout the world;
how can I be so humiliated by a single word as to become someone else's disciple?"
Having thought this, he was displeased.
The Master, knowing his mind, immediately ordered him to enter the room and manifested various transformations through his supernormal powers.
Knowing that the Master’s mind was not yet settled, he joyfully submitted and reflected:
"It is only natural that I am his disciple. He thought further:
"The Master’s words say that your talent and clarity are extraordinary; it is simply that you have not yet reached perfection."
If one studies the Dharma I have attained,
one will deeply penetrate the faculties, powers, factors of awakening, and eloquence,
and clearly discern its underlying meaning.
He was such that no one in the world could rival him.
The Master returned to his own country, while the disciple remained in Central India (Madhyadeśa).
He was extensively versed in all the scriptures and attained profound mastery of both Buddhist and non-Buddhist teachings.
His eloquence surpassed that of his contemporaries, and the fourfold assembly revered and submitted to him.
The King of India treated him with great esteem.
Later, there was the King of the Lesser Yuezhi in Northern India.
Having launched an attack on the Chinese capital and besieged it for an extended period,
the King of Central India sent an envoy with this message:
"If you have any requests, we shall provide them to you."
"Why trouble the people so much by staying here for so long?
He replied, "If you submit your will, I shall send three hundred million gold pieces and grant you amnesty.
The king said, "Even taking this entire kingdom together, there is not even one hundred million gold pieces."
"How can three hundred million [gold pieces] be obtained?
He replied, "In your kingdom there are two great treasures:
first, the Buddha’s bowl; second, the bhikṣu Prajñākūṭa."
"Give these to me, and they shall be worth twenty million pieces of gold.
The king said, "I hold these two treasures very dear and cannot bear to part with them.
Thereupon, the bhikṣu preached the Dharma for the king.
The inscription reads:
"Among those who harbor feelings and undergo transformation, none in the world can rival them.
The Buddha-way is profound and vast, its principle residing in universal salvation."
The virtue of a great man likewise takes the salvation of all things as its highest priority.
Because the worldly teachings face many difficulties, the royal transformation of the people is limited to a single state.
Now, by widely proclaiming the Buddha-way, you may become a Dharma King over the four seas.
Regarding the principle of a bhikṣu ordaining others, there should be no room for difference; the merit lies within the mind, regardless of whether it is far or near.
One ought to maintain a vast and lofty perspective—why need it be limited to what is before one's eyes?
The King, who had long revered and esteemed him, accepted his words with respect.
He gave it to him immediately, and the King of Mo-ti returned to his own country.
His ministers deliberated, saying: "It was indeed fitting that the King should honor the Buddha’s bowl.
As for a bhikṣu, he is worth one hundred million pieces of gold throughout the world."
"Is this not perhaps excessive?
King Shenxiu knows that the bhikṣu is of lofty character, eminent and far-reaching in understanding;
his guidance and benefit are vast and profound, and his eloquence in preaching the Dharma has even moved non-human beings."
Desiring to awaken the various deluded masses,
he fasted for seven horses' lengths of fodder until the dawn of the sixth day;
he then gathered all the śramaṇas and heterodox practitioners from both within and without, and invited the bhikṣus to preach the Dharma.
All who heard were enlightened.

The king tied this horse before the assembly and gave it grass; because the horse was fond of floating grass, he gave it floating grass. The horse shed tears as it listened to the Dharma, having no thought of eating.
Thereupon, the world realized that he was no ordinary being;
because he explained the meaning through the medium of horses,
he was consequently named Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa.
He widely proclaimed the Buddha-dharma in Northern India,
guiding and benefiting all living beings with skillful means;
he enabled people to fulfill their meritorious virtues and was revered by the fourfold assembly.
Furthermore, they were all collectively called "Sun of Merit.
(From the *Biography of Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa*)
